Repo /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper. Stacked follow-up to the speed work. Base: the LOCAL branch `worktree-agent-aed2d7748791ef6ec` (head 4c59ef11, 6 commits: merge memo, kept props, two programs + converter threads, tests, docs+changeset, lint fixes; only the first 3 are on origin as perf/checker-extract-speed 854da4c6 because Entire's pre-push hook panics on today's nightly (nil pointer in checkpoint.readFoldsCase): do NOT use --no-verify, never bypass hooks; commit locally in small signed commits and TRY `git push origin HEAD:perf/checker-shared-bases` at the end; if the hook still panics, report that the commits are local only and stop). Create your branch from that local ref: `git switch -c perf/checker-shared-bases worktree-agent-aed2d7748791ef6ec` (in your own worktree you may need `git checkout -b perf/checker-shared-bases 4c59ef11`). Read the previous worker's profile in docs/gate-measurements.md (new subsection), scratch in ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/extract-speed/ (ab.sh, measure.py, prof.py, samply profiles, builds caliper-l1..l5c3), and docs/type-checker-integration.md, ADR 0026.

Context: whole-project `extract` with the built-in checker is now 1.82 s gate-large / 1.37 s Chakra-only (RDT 7.25 / 4.10 s), peak RSS 1,077 / 870 MiB (1,477 MiB at 3x components: memory grows with component count). Floor per checker lane ~1.1 s on Chakra, half of it JSON in `getPropertiesOfType` (787 calls, 288 MB JSON out, every declaration carries its full path) and `getTypesOfSymbols` (80 MB). Caliper's side owns the memory (checker arenas only ~46 MiB). tsrs_api 0.24 has no typed in-process entry; do NOT fork or vendor tsrs.

Do, MEASURE FIRST for each, keep only changes with a measured gain, one commit per lever:
(1) Shared base types: measure how much of the 288 MB / requests is the same base types (HTML attributes, style props, React terminals) re-asked per component (count by type id / base declaration). If large, ask the checker for a base type's properties ONCE per snapshot (cache keyed by type handle + the question) and per component ask only for own/derived members, composing inherited ones exactly as the checker would (overrides, optionality changes, intersections, mapped/conditional types, generics instantiated differently, index signatures, JSDoc provenance, `is_own`/declaration provenance). Correctness is mandatory: where composition cannot be shown identical, fall back to asking for the full type. Prove with a FULL-CONTENT diff (parse JSON, drop stats, compare) against the base on gate-large and Chakra-only, the construct checker lane, `construct:parity`, determinism (gate_harness determinism with subprocess thread variants), and new tests that fail when the key/composition is made coarser.
(2) Whole-program answer cache on disk for `extract` (and nothing else): persist the checker's per-component answers keyed by a hash of EVERY file the program read (plus tsrs pin, options, Caliper schema version); any change anywhere invalidates the whole cache (conservative by construction; do NOT attempt per-component closures, ADR 0026 lists those as unsolved). A rerun with no changes should cost close to `--no-checker` time. Where does the existing on-disk cache live and why did the weekly measure that it does not shorten the checker pass? Reuse that cache mechanism and schema versioning; no new option unless unavoidable; `--no-cache` still bypasses. Tests: warm hit, invalidation on edit of a file the program read, on tsrs pin change, on option change, determinism of cached vs fresh output (byte-identical).
(3) Memory: intern declaration/path strings at parse time and parse the checker's JSON with borrowed slices (zero-copy) in the converter path (JSON parse was 0.6 s of Caliper's thread; every declaration allocates a path String); stream `extract` output component by component instead of holding every answer until the end (peak RSS must stay flat as component count grows: re-measure gate-x3 2,814 components, was 1,477 MiB); free the per-run prop cache after components are written in one-shot `extract` (Storybook sessions keep it); check whether the CLI uses mimalloc like the napi binding and measure it (RSS and time) before changing anything. Report peak RSS before/after for gate-large, Chakra-only and gate-x3; keep peak RSS under 2 GB everywhere and prefer lower.
Success: report the new times and RSS vs the 1.82 / 1.37 s and 1,077 / 870 MiB baseline (3 interleaved runs, medians, same harness as before), byte-identical output (full-content diff) on both projects in default and weekly settings, all gates green. If a lever shows no gain, drop it and say so with the number. If something needs an upstream tsrs change, say exactly what.
Rules: scratch in ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/extract-speed/ (no /tmp); no oracle, no corpus fetches; no new scripts/options/recipes unless wired into CI/weekly; update docs/gate-measurements.md, docs/measurement.md (RDT ratio stays measured, not asserted), docs/type-checker-integration.md, changeset as fits. Rust 1.99.1 toolchain first on PATH (/Users/gabe/.rustup/toolchains/1.99.1-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin), outside the sandbox where needed, `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile` in the worktree if needed. Signed commits with trailer `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013R2ytvK9B32ZaSUaSe6aAZ`. Do not open the PR, do not poll CI. Final report: the measurements per lever (before/after), what was kept/dropped and why, correctness proof results, SHAs and whether the push worked, what was not verified.

#!/bin/zsh
# Usage: ab.sh <runs> <binary>... — interleaved whole-project extract (--json --quiet --no-cache) on gate-large and
# Chakra-only, wall seconds and peak RSS MiB from /usr/bin/time -l, one line per run.
runs=$1; shift
cd /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/extract-speed
for i in $(seq $runs); do
  for bin in "$@"; do
    for project in gate-large chakra-only; do
      case $project in
        gate-large) src=../gate-large/src ;;
        chakra-only) src=../checker-default/chakra-only/src ;;
      esac
      out=$(/usr/bin/time -l $bin extract --src $src --json --quiet --no-cache 2>&1 >/dev/null)
      real=$(echo "$out" | awk '/real/ {print $1}')
      rss=$(echo "$out" | awk '/maximum resident/ {printf "%d", $1/1048576}')
      echo "$project $(basename $bin) ${real}s ${rss}MiB load=$(sysctl -n vm.loadavg | awk '{print $2}')"
    done
  done
done
"""RDT against Caliper on gate-large and Chakra-only with the weekly's own helpers (program_inputs, run_once), interleaved.

Usage: python3 measure.py <repo> <runs> <tool>... where a tool is rdt, or name=path/to/caliper-docgen[:extra args]
"""
import json
import os
import sys
import tempfile

repo = sys.argv[1]
runs = int(sys.argv[2])
tools = sys.argv[3:]
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(repo, 'scripts'))
import corpora  # noqa: E402
import weekly  # noqa: E402

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
PROJECTS = {
    'gate-large': os.path.expanduser('~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large/src'),
    'chakra-only': os.path.expanduser('~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/checker-default/chakra-only/src'),
}
only = os.environ.get('PROJECTS')
if only:
    PROJECTS = {k: v for k, v in PROJECTS.items() if k in only.split(',')}

results = {}
for name, src in PROJECTS.items():
    work = os.path.join(HERE, 'rdt-inputs')
    os.makedirs(work, exist_ok=True)
    list_file, tsconfig = weekly.program_inputs(name, src, work)
    for run in range(runs):
        for tool in tools:
            if tool == 'rdt':
                out = os.path.join(work, f'{name}.rdt.json')
                command = ['node', '--max-old-space-size=8192', os.path.join(repo, 'scripts', 'rdt.mjs'), list_file, tsconfig, out]
                seconds, rss = corpora.run_once(command)
                with open(out) as f:
                    count = len(json.load(f)['components'])
                extra = f'components={count}'
            else:
                label, _, rest = tool.partition('=')
                binary, _, args = rest.partition(':')
                command = [binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json', '--quiet'] + (args.split() if args else [])
                with tempfile.TemporaryFile() as out:
                    seconds, rss = corpora.run_once(command, stdout=out)
                    extra = f'bytes={out.tell()}'
                tool = label
            line = {'project': name, 'tool': tool, 'run': run, 's': round(seconds, 3), 'rss_mib': round(rss), 'extra': extra,
                    'load': os.getloadavg()[0]}
            print(json.dumps(line), flush=True)
            results.setdefault((name, tool), []).append((seconds, rss))

for (name, tool), samples in results.items():
    secs = sorted(s for s, _ in samples)
    print(f'{name:12} {tool:24} median {secs[len(secs) // 2]:.2f}s range {secs[0]:.2f}-{secs[-1]:.2f} rss max {max(r for _, r in samples):.0f}')
#!/bin/zsh
# Usage: same.sh <binary> [extra args] — runs extract on gate-large and Chakra-only, drops `stats`, and compares the
# bytes with the reference made by the base binary (ref-<project>.json, made on the first call with REF=1).
bin=$1; shift
cd /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/extract-speed
for project in gate-large chakra-only; do
  case $project in
    gate-large) src=../gate-large/src ;;
    chakra-only) src=../checker-default/chakra-only/src ;;
  esac
  $bin extract --src $src --json --quiet --no-cache "$@" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); d.pop("stats",None); sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(d,sort_keys=False))' > out-$project$SUFFIX.json
  if [[ -n $REF ]]; then cp out-$project$SUFFIX.json ref-$project$SUFFIX.json; fi
  if cmp -s out-$project$SUFFIX.json ref-$project$SUFFIX.json; then echo "$project same ($(wc -c < out-$project$SUFFIX.json) bytes)"; else echo "$project DIFFERS"; fi
done

# Runs a command with the Rust 1.99.1 toolchain first on PATH.

#!/bin/zsh
# Usage: gates.sh <rounds> <gate> [args...] — runs gate_harness <gate> on gate-large with the built-in checker,
# base then head, interleaved, printing each JSON line's scalar fields.
rounds=$1; gate=$2; shift 2
cd /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/extract-speed
for i in $(seq $rounds); do
  for h in base head; do
    echo -n "$h "
    ./harness-$h $gate --src ../gate-large/src --tsc built-in "$@" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.loads(sys.stdin.read()); print({k:v for k,v in d.items() if not isinstance(v,list)})'
  done
done
#!/bin/zsh
# Runs the repository's gates in turn with the Rust 1.99.1 toolchain, one log each, and prints each exit code.
export PATH=/Users/gabe/.rustup/toolchains/1.99.1-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin:$PATH
cd /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper/.claude/worktrees/agent-aed2d7748791ef6ec
logs=/Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/extract-speed/checks
mkdir -p $logs
for gate in "lint doc-check machete typos" deny semver test-rust test-checker-lane test-ts test-napi; do
  name=${gate// /-}
  just ${=gate} > $logs/$name.log 2>&1
  echo "$gate exit=$?"
done
pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:parity > $logs/parity.log 2>&1
echo "construct:parity exit=$?"
cargo nextest run -p caliper-docgen-semantic -p caliper-docgen-core > $logs/nextest.log 2>&1
echo "nextest semantic+core exit=$?"

73	## The checker is the default (S8)
74	
75	S8 turns the checker on by default (`--no-checker` and `checker: false` turn it off). Measured 2026-11-12 on `feat/checker-is-default` against `main` at `8212aef8`, release builds, the built-in checker (tsrs crates `0.24.0`), macOS 27.3 on an Apple M5 Max, a shared machine at load 8 to 21. Scratch inputs are under `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/checker-default`.
76	
77	- **Whole-project `extract`** (`extract --src <dir> --json --quiet --no-cache`, otherwise the CLI's defaults; wall time and peak RSS from `time -l`, 3 interleaved runs each, ranges):
78	  - `gate-large`, 938 Chakra and MUI wrappers: **6.05 to 10.56 s, 966 to 974 MiB** by default (the 10.56 s run was the first, at the highest load; the other two 6.05 s). `--no-checker`: 0.09 to 0.10 s, 201 to 203 MiB. `main` gave 0.09 to 0.10 s and 196 to 198 MiB by default, and 6.18 to 8.33 s and 968 to 973 MiB with `--experimental-semantic-types`.
79	  - The 787 Chakra wrappers alone: **5.37 to 5.55 s, 765 to 776 MiB** by default; `--no-checker` 0.07 to 0.08 s, 158 MiB; `main`'s `--experimental-semantic-types` 5.37 to 5.50 s, 759 to 772 MiB.
80	  - Three renamed copies of `gate-large` (2,814 components, one run): 15.4 s and 1,053 MiB by default, 0.14 s and 228 MiB with `--no-checker`. Memory hardly grows with the component count: the whole-project pass holds one program and interns equal props across components, so no `extract` measured here comes near 2 GB.
81	  - Output: the default's canonical JSON equals `main`'s `--experimental-semantic-types` once `stats` is set aside, and `--no-checker`'s equals `main`'s default but for one help text (`OPAQUE_TYPE`'s hint now names `--no-checker`).
82	  - Not measured: the five corpora of `docs/measurement.md`, which are not installed here (no corpus was fetched for this).
83	- **Weekly, bench and agent eval.** They run the default from `feat/weekly-checker-default` on (they passed `--no-checker` until then). The fixtures above, re-measured on that branch (default settings, `--no-cache`), are in `docs/measurement.md` ("The budgets"): `gate-large` 5.80 to 6.35 s and 967 to 986 MiB, Chakra alone 5.22 to 5.41 s and 760 to 777 MiB, three copies 14.7 to 15.2 s and 1,046 to 1,050 MiB. The five corpora's budgets are "record on first run".
84	- **A session's kept answers** (the Storybook addon's configuration through the native binding: lazy, dependencies loaded, nothing collapsed, `semanticWaitMs` and `semanticWaitEmptyMs` 60 s so every answer is the checker's; `gate-large`'s components asked one at a time, the process's RSS read every 100). Each checker answer is kept for the next request, and each held its own copy of every prop: 1,257, 1,930 and 2,602 MiB after 100, 200 and 300 components, about 6.7 MiB per Chakra component (trail 369 slice 2 read 5,365 MiB at 900). With the checker on by default a session that asked for every story would run out of memory, so the answer cache now shares one copy of each equal prop per generation (`AnswerCache::shared` in `crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs`), as the whole-project merge does: 716, 786 and 825 MiB at 100, 200 and 300, **1,007 MiB after all 938, peak 1,058 MiB**. The structural session alone (`checker: false`) peaks at 377 MiB.
85	- **Budgets, per trail 333.** The first answer keeps its 150 ms budget for a story that was prefetched or answered before (the addon's `prefetchStories`, then the kept answer); the cold first answer is recorded rather than gated: `ChakraButton` median **171 ms** in process (169 to 173, trail 369 slice 2), against 277 ms over the pipe. Watch keeps 25 ms for the checker's own part (own props: p95 6.3 ms in process), and records the `ButtonProps` form: **p95 162.3 ms** (p50 157.7, p99 168.5), whose floor is converting its 1,138 props.
86	
87	### Whole-project `extract` against react-docgen-typescript (2026-11-12, `perf/checker-extract-speed`)
88	
89	- **Same harness.** `scripts/weekly.py`'s own helpers: `program_inputs` (every `.tsx` under `src`, its tsconfig) and `scripts/rdt.mjs` for RDT (`react-docgen-typescript` 2.4.0 from `apps/oracle`, `node --max-old-space-size=8192`), `corpora.run_once` for wall time and peak RSS of each process; Caliper `extract --src <dir> --json --quiet --no-cache`. Three interleaved runs of each, medians, release builds, macOS 27.3 on an Apple M5 Max at load 4 to 6; scratch in `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/extract-speed`.
90	- **Before** (`feat/checker-is-default`, `dc27edd7`): `gate-large` (938 components) **6.16 s**, 977 MiB, against RDT's **7.25 s** (7.21 to 7.78), 3,884 MiB: 1.2 times RDT's speed. Chakra alone (787) **5.73 s**, 779 MiB, against RDT's **4.10 s** (3.93 to 4.23), 3,221 MiB: slower than RDT. `--no-checker`: 0.10 s and 0.08 s.
91	- **Where the 6 s went** (`gate-large`, `samply`, 1 ms samples). 0.17 s structural pass and program; 3.9 s answering, during which caliper's thread was busy 3.3 s (converting 1.1 s, interning each component's copy of each prop 0.8 s, copying converted types out of the memo about 1 s, parsing the checker's JSON 0.6 s, declarations 0.4 s) and waited 0.6 s, while the checker's one thread was busy 2.2 s of it (0.3 s of that writing JSON); then **1.8 s merging** the answer into the output, every component's every prop copied, reordered, hashed and interned again (Chakra's components share about a thousand style props). The run sent 75,000 requests (26,000 `getTypesOfType`, 14,500 `getTypeArguments`, 10,600 `typeToString`, 5,500 `getBaseTypes`); the type memo had 1.09 million hits and 55,000 misses. In process, on Chakra alone, the checker's time is mostly two requests per component: `getPropertiesOfType` (787 requests, 667 ms, 288 MB of JSON out: each props type's thousand properties, every declaration with its full path) and `getTypesOfSymbols` (939, 344 ms, 80 MB out, 42 MB of symbol references in); then `getTypesOfType` (22,600, 223 ms) and nothing else above 60 ms.
92	- **What changed, each measured after the last** (medians, `gate-large` / Chakra alone):
93	  - The whole-project merge makes a prop once per checker prop, structural prop, written union and code default (each a shared copy, kept by address while the merge runs; `MergeMemo` in `crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs`): 6.2 s to **4.6 s** on `gate-large`.
94	  - The converter keeps each prop it answered for the snapshot by what makes it (`PropKey`: the property's name, optionality, declarations and parent, its type's handle, which JSDoc is asked), so a later component converts, copies and interns only the props it does not share: **2.8 s / 2.1 s**.
95	  - The run converts on four threads (`CONVERTER_THREADS`) instead of one: **2.35 s / 1.75 s**. The checker's thread was then busy 95% of the run.
96	  - Two programs over the same root files in one snapshot, each on a checker thread of its own (`CHECKER_PROGRAMS`; each program's requests go down one lane, since `tsrs_api` locks a program's one checker per request, and one shared queue first let both threads wait on the same lock), with the files handed to whichever worker is free: **1.73 s / 1.40 s**. Peak RSS grew by about 80 MiB, so the parsed files are shared; each program converts the shared types again.
97	  - Tried and not kept: three programs, 1.70 s / 1.32 s against two's 1.82 / 1.37 in the same series, for 85 MiB and more CPU, and slower than two at load 30 to 40. Not done: skipping the JSON in process (`tsrs_api` 0.24 has no public typed entry: its `CheckerHost` for a session is private, so `Session::handle_request` with JSON text is the only door); answering from the on-disk cache (ADR 0026's dependency closure is still unsolved, so no invalidation could be shown conservative); skipping requests whose answer looks known (nothing measured asks for less without a new proof).
98	- **After** (`854da4c6`, same series as the before): `gate-large` **1.82 s** (1.69 to 2.02), 1,077 MiB: **4.0 times** RDT's speed; Chakra alone **1.37 s** (1.32 to 1.38), 870 MiB: **3.0 times** RDT's. With the weekly's settings (`--load-dependencies --collapse-inherited-props none`, cache on) 1.84 s / 1.46 s, 1,160 / 970 MiB. Three renamed copies of `gate-large` (2,814 components, one run): 4.15 s and 1,477 MiB against 17.4 s and 1,047 MiB; memory now grows with the component count (the merge holds the structural props it merged over until it ends, and two programs hold their own types), still under 2 GB.
99	- **Same answer.** The canonical JSON with `stats` set aside is byte-identical to the base's on `gate-large` and Chakra alone, in the default and the weekly settings, over repeated runs. `gate_harness determinism --tsc built-in` passes (nine outputs of 399,060,458 bytes, 1, 2 and 4 threads, each in a fresh process, reversed order included); `memory` passes on both (650 of 650 the checker's, none stale, the last equal to a fresh session's). First answer (`ChakraButton`, 5 runs, two interleaved rounds) 176 and 183 ms against the base's 177 and 176; watch's `ButtonProps` form p50 / p95 165 / 220 ms against the base's 166 / 234 in the same round (the Storybook session asks one program and gains only the prop and merge sharing). `crates/semantic/src/lib.rs` holds three programs to one program's answer, a global augmentation in one file included, and a kept prop to the JSDoc its component asked for; `crates/core/src/types/semantic/tests.rs` holds the merge memo to each component's structural prop.
100	- **The floor now.** Each checker thread is busy about 1.1 s on Chakra alone: the two requests above, half of whose time is writing and reading JSON. A `tsrs` request that answers a type's properties with their types, without each declaration's full path, or a public in-process entry that skips the JSON, is what would take the next large step; both are upstream changes.
101	
102	## Startup prefetch (trail 332)
103	
104	- **The gate.** In a real Storybook 11 run on Chakra, the first story has the checker's props within 150 ms of the browser's request when the prefetch started at least as long before it as the component's cold cost; a story outside the prefetch is no slower than without it; peak memory at most 30 MB above.
105	- **How it reaches Storybook.** Storybook 11 starts its docgen worker on the first `extractDocgen` (`createDocgenWorkerClient`: `worker ??= new DocgenWorker`), so nothing in the worker runs earlier. The addon's preset adds an `experimental_devServer` hook, which Storybook applies before the builders start; after Storybook's own hook registers the `core/docgen` service, it reads the story index and calls `getService('core/docgen', { internal: true }).commands.extractDocgen({ id })` (`storybook/internal/core-server`, internal API, Storybook `11.0.0-alpha.9`) for the opening story's component. The command runs the provider chain and writes the answer to the service's state, which the manager receives with its first sync. The manager's Controls panel subscribes once the story is prepared; that subscription's load calls `extractDocgen` again, so the provider is asked a second time and answers from the session, but `isInitialLoading` is false while the stored payload is there, so the panel shows it at once.
106	- **Harness.** `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/prefetch`: `storybook dev` (11.0.0-alpha.9, Vite 8, `@storybook/builder-vite` 10.6.2 from the pnpm store with its mock extraction stubbed, since the store has no 11 builder) over 40 stories of `gate-large`'s Chakra wrappers with a `ChakraProvider` decorator, `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'` on the pinned tsrs and `fallback: 'never'`. Playwright opens the root URL as soon as `index.json` answers, as `storybook dev` opens the browser once the index is built. The browser's request and answer times are the manager's websocket frames (`services:command-invoke` for `extractDocgen`, the `core/docgen` state entry); a provider registered after the addon's logs each request in the worker. Shared machine at load 20 to 160; 13 runs with the prefetch (9 of one story, 4 of three) and 9 without, interleaved.
107	- **Lead time.** The browser asked 1.5 to 6.3 s after the server was spawned (median 2.2 s), 0.8 to 2.3 s after the prefetch started (median 1.2 s); the prefetch starts 45 to 120 ms after the index is built. `ChakraButton` cold through the prefetch took 0.57 to 2.2 s (median 1.0 s): the opening story fits before the browser asks, a second large component does not.
108	- **Result.** In every run where the prefetch started at least its cold cost before the request (9 runs, and one whose prefetch start was not logged), the checker's 1,137 props were in the browser from 84 ms before to 92 ms after its request (median 10 ms before). Where it had not (3 runs at high load), they arrived 246 to 308 ms after it. Without the prefetch they arrived 0.74 to 2.9 s after the request (median 1.6 s), and once, at load 159, the story got 0 props after its 2 s wait. **PASS.**
109	- **A story outside the prefetch.** Opened 10 s later: 0.45 to 1.4 s with (median 0.82 s) against 0.64 to 2.1 s without (median 1.0 s). Opened directly at startup, competing with the prefetch: 0.5 to 2.2 s with (median 1.1 s) against 0.82 to 1.7 s without (median 1.35 s). **PASS** in the median; the slowest single value is with the prefetch, at the highest load.
110	- **Memory.** The Storybook process tree (Node and tsrs), opening the first story: peak 752 to 825 MiB with one story prefetched (median 767) against 720 to 764 without (median 750): **+17 MiB** by median, +22 in each of the two interleaved series; at idle 10 s later within noise. Prefetching 3 stories held about 200 MiB more at idle and made a story opened at startup slower (median 2.2 s), which is why the default is 1.
111	- **Found on the way.** Storybook hands a preset its own options merged with the addon's; its own `cache` (a file-system cache object) reached the native session as the addon's `cache`, which it refused, so the addon could not start in any real `storybook dev` until the preset dropped a non-boolean `cache`. And with the default `fallback: 'degraded'`, `ChakraButton` is handed to React's docgen even when the checker answers, because the structural warning that `Button` was not found stays on the answer.
112	
113	## Not covered
114	
115	- Other platforms: both measurements ran on macOS arm64. The Linux CI run is a separate gate.
116	- Wall time was not part of the question; a run takes about 0.5 s per edit here.
117	- The per-edit `ps` sampling reads the answering process after its reply, so a process that peaked inside a request and shrank before the sample is under-read.

  - The run converts on four threads (`CONVERTER_THREADS`) instead of one: **2.35 s / 1.75 s**. The checker's thread was then busy 95% of the run.
  - Two programs over the same root files in one snapshot, each on a checker thread of its own (`CHECKER_PROGRAMS`; each program's requests go down one lane, since `tsrs_api` locks a program's one checker per request, and one shared queue first let both threads wait on the same lock), with the files handed to whichever worker is free: **1.73 s / 1.40 s**. Peak RSS grew by about 80 MiB, so the parsed files are shared; each program converts the shared types again.
  - Tried and not kept: three programs, 1.70 s / 1.32 s against two's 1.82 / 1.37 in the same series, for 85 MiB and more CPU, and slower than two at load 30 to 40. Not done: skipping the JSON in process (`tsrs_api` 0.24 has no public typed entry: its `CheckerHost` for a session is private, so `Session::handle_request` with JSON text is the only door); answering from the on-disk cache (ADR 0026's dependency closure is still unsolved, so no invalidation could be shown conservative); skipping requests whose answer looks known (nothing measured asks for less without a new proof).
- **After** (`854da4c6`, same series as the before): `gate-large` **1.82 s** (1.69 to 2.02), 1,077 MiB: **4.0 times** RDT's speed; Chakra alone **1.37 s** (1.32 to 1.38), 870 MiB: **3.0 times** RDT's. With the weekly's settings (`--load-dependencies --collapse-inherited-props none`, cache on) 1.84 s / 1.46 s, 1,160 / 970 MiB. Three renamed copies of `gate-large` (2,814 components, one run): 4.15 s and 1,477 MiB against 17.4 s and 1,047 MiB; memory now grows with the component count (the merge holds the structural props it merged over until it ends, and two programs hold their own types), still under 2 GB.
- **Same answer.** The canonical JSON with `stats` set aside is byte-identical to the base's on `gate-large` and Chakra alone, in the default and the weekly settings, over repeated runs. `gate_harness determinism --tsc built-in` passes (nine outputs of 399,060,458 bytes, 1, 2 and 4 threads, each in a fresh process, reversed order included); `memory` passes on both (650 of 650 the checker's, none stale, the last equal to a fresh session's). First answer (`ChakraButton`, 5 runs, two interleaved rounds) 176 and 183 ms against the base's 177 and 176; watch's `ButtonProps` form p50 / p95 165 / 220 ms against the base's 166 / 234 in the same round (the Storybook session asks one program and gains only the prop and merge sharing). `crates/semantic/src/lib.rs` holds three programs to one program's answer, a global augmentation in one file included, and a kept prop to the JSDoc its component asked for; `crates/core/src/types/semantic/tests.rs` holds the merge memo to each component's structural prop.
- **The floor now.** Each checker thread is busy about 1.1 s on Chakra alone: the two requests above, half of whose time is writing and reading JSON. A `tsrs` request that answers a type's properties with their types, without each declaration's full path, or a public in-process entry that skips the JSON, is what would take the next large step; both are upstream changes.

## Startup prefetch (trail 332)

- **The gate.** In a real Storybook 11 run on Chakra, the first story has the checker's props within 150 ms of the browser's request when the prefetch started at least as long before it as the component's cold cost; a story outside the prefetch is no slower than without it; peak memory at most 30 MB above.
- **How it reaches Storybook.** Storybook 11 starts its docgen worker on the first `extractDocgen` (`createDocgenWorkerClient`: `worker ??= new DocgenWorker`), so nothing in the worker runs earlier. The addon's preset adds an `experimental_devServer` hook, which Storybook applies before the builders start; after Storybook's own hook registers the `core/docgen` service, it reads the story index and calls `getService('core/docgen', { internal: true }).commands.extractDocgen({ id })` (`storybook/internal/core-server`, internal API, Storybook `11.0.0-alpha.9`) for the opening story's component. The command runs the provider chain and writes the answer to the service's state, which the manager receives with its first sync. The manager's Controls panel subscribes once the story is prepared; that subscription's load calls `extractDocgen` again, so the provider is asked a second time and answers from the session, but `isInitialLoading` is false while the stored payload is there, so the panel shows it at once.
- **Harness.** `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/prefetch`: `storybook dev` (11.0.0-alpha.9, Vite 8, `@storybook/builder-vite` 10.6.2 from the pnpm store with its mock extraction stubbed, since the store has no 11 builder) over 40 stories of `gate-large`'s Chakra wrappers with a `ChakraProvider` decorator, `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'` on the pinned tsrs and `fallback: 'never'`. Playwright opens the root URL as soon as `index.json` answers, as `storybook dev` opens the browser once the index is built. The browser's request and answer times are the manager's websocket frames (`services:command-invoke` for `extractDocgen`, the `core/docgen` state entry); a provider registered after the addon's logs each request in the worker. Shared machine at load 20 to 160; 13 runs with the prefetch (9 of one story, 4 of three) and 9 without, interleaved.
- **Lead time.** The browser asked 1.5 to 6.3 s after the server was spawned (median 2.2 s), 0.8 to 2.3 s after the prefetch started (median 1.2 s); the prefetch starts 45 to 120 ms after the index is built. `ChakraButton` cold through the prefetch took 0.57 to 2.2 s (median 1.0 s): the opening story fits before the browser asks, a second large component does not.
- **Result.** In every run where the prefetch started at least its cold cost before the request (9 runs, and one whose prefetch start was not logged), the checker's 1,137 props were in the browser from 84 ms before to 92 ms after its request (median 10 ms before). Where it had not (3 runs at high load), they arrived 246 to 308 ms after it. Without the prefetch they arrived 0.74 to 2.9 s after the request (median 1.6 s), and once, at load 159, the story got 0 props after its 2 s wait. **PASS.**
- **A story outside the prefetch.** Opened 10 s later: 0.45 to 1.4 s with (median 0.82 s) against 0.64 to 2.1 s without (median 1.0 s). Opened directly at startup, competing with the prefetch: 0.5 to 2.2 s with (median 1.1 s) against 0.82 to 1.7 s without (median 1.35 s). **PASS** in the median; the slowest single value is with the prefetch, at the highest load.
- **Memory.** The Storybook process tree (Node and tsrs), opening the first story: peak 752 to 825 MiB with one story prefetched (median 767) against 720 to 764 without (median 750): **+17 MiB** by median, +22 in each of the two interleaved series; at idle 10 s later within noise. Prefetching 3 stories held about 200 MiB more at idle and made a story opened at startup slower (median 2.2 s), which is why the default is 1.
- **Found on the way.** Storybook hands a preset its own options merged with the addon's; its own `cache` (a file-system cache object) reached the native session as the addon's `cache`, which it refused, so the addon could not start in any real `storybook dev` until the preset dropped a non-boolean `cache`. And with the default `fallback: 'degraded'`, `ChakraButton` is handed to React's docgen even when the checker answers, because the structural warning that `Button` was not found stays on the answer.

## Not covered

- Other platforms: both measurements ran on macOS arm64. The Linux CI run is a separate gate.
- Wall time was not part of the question; a run takes about 0.5 s per edit here.
- The per-edit `ps` sampling reads the answering process after its reply, so a process that peaked inside a request and shrank before the sample is under-read.

"""Medians of ab.sh lines from stdin, per project and binary: wall, peak RSS, CPU."""
import sys, collections, statistics
d = collections.defaultdict(list)
for line in sys.stdin:
    parts = line.split()
    if len(parts) < 5 or not parts[2].endswith('s'):
        continue
    print(line, end='')
    d[(parts[0], parts[1])].append((float(parts[2][:-1]), int(parts[3][:-3]), float(parts[4][4:-1])))
for (project, binary), runs in sorted(d.items()):
    w, r, c = zip(*runs)
    print(f'{project:12} {binary:16} wall {statistics.median(w):.2f}s ({min(w):.2f}-{max(w):.2f})  rss {statistics.median(r):.0f} MiB  cpu {statistics.median(c):.2f}s  n={len(runs)}')

Two packages provide one:
docs/type-checker-integration.md:106:The protocol detail that matters for `tsrs` is unchanged from `typescript`: the client sends `createPrograms[].compilerOptions` (the Node client sends `options`; the server accepts both, and `crates/semantic/tests/replay.rs` pins the key). The tests that ask a real checker (`tsrs_real`, `cases`, `families`, `declared`, `memo`, `exports`, `composes`, `instantiate`, `watch`, and `on_demand`'s real-checker tests) ask the built-in one; `TSRS_BIN` (a `tsrs` binary) or `CALIPER_TEST_TSC` (the Go `bin/tsc`, for `instantiate`, `watch`, `composes` and `on_demand`) runs them on that process instead. Replay tests stay on the process route: handles are numbered process-wide, so a recording does not replay in a second in-process session.

"""One whole run of a Node tool that writes its components to `out`: wall ms, peak RSS MiB and the components."""
    seconds, rss = run_once(command)
    with open(out) as f:
        return {'ms': round(seconds * 1000), 'rss_mib': round(rss)}, json.load(f)['components']


def caliper_run(binary, src, runs):
    """Median wall ms and largest peak RSS MiB of `extract --json` in the Storybook addon's configuration (dependencies
    loaded, inherited props not collapsed), and the JSON's size. The checker answers, as
    it does by default (docs/measurement.md)."""
    command = [binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json', '--load-dependencies', '--collapse-inherited-props', 'none']
    with tempfile.TemporaryFile() as out:
        run_once(command, stdout=out)
        size = out.tell()
    samples = [run_once(command) for _ in range(runs)]
    return {'ms': round(statistics.median(s for s, _ in samples) * 1000), 'rss_mib': round(max(r for _, r in samples)),
            'json_mb': round(size / 2**20, 2)}


def caliper_components(binary, src, root):
    """Caliper's components in RDT's format, as (file, name) -> prop names."""
    command = [binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--format', 'rdt', '--html-attributes', 'full', '--include-unexported',
               '--quiet', '--load-dependencies', '--collapse-inherited-props', 'none']
    out = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    return {(relative(c['filePath'], root), norm_name(c['displayName'])): set(c['props'])
            for c in json.loads(out[out.index('{'):]).values()}


def caliper_layer_members(binary, src, root):
    """The props Caliper's collapsed inheritance layers hold, as (file, name) -> prop names: the output names them in a
    layer instead of listing them as props, and the canonical JSON is the one that carries the layers."""
    command = [binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json', '--html-attributes', 'full', '--include-unexported', '--quiet',
               '--load-dependencies', '--collapse-inherited-props', 'none']
    out = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    document = schema_version.check(json.loads(out[out.index('{'):]), 'weekly')
    lists = document.get('nameLists', {})
    members = {}
    for c in document['components'].values():
        names = set()
        for layer in c.get('inheritance', []):
            if layer.get('members'):
                names |= set(lists[layer['members']])
        members[(relative(c['filePath'], root), norm_name(c['displayName']))] = names
    return members

#!/bin/zsh
# Usage: kept.sh <binary> <runs> [extra args] — on gate-large and Chakra-only, a fresh --cache-dir per project: one cold
# run that keeps the checker's answer, then <runs> warm runs; wall s and peak RSS of each, and whether each output equals
# the reference (ref-<project>$SUFFIX.json, stats set aside).
bin=$1; runs=$2; shift 2
cd /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/extract-speed
for project in gate-large chakra-only; do
  case $project in
    gate-large) src=../gate-large/src ;;
    chakra-only) src=../checker-default/chakra-only/src ;;
  esac
  cache=kept-cache/$project
  rm -rf $cache
  for i in $(seq 0 $runs); do
    out=$(/usr/bin/time -l $bin extract --src $src --json --quiet --cache-dir $cache "$@" 2>time.err | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); d.pop("stats",None); sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(d,sort_keys=False))')
    real=$(awk '/real/ {print $1}' time.err)
    rss=$(awk '/maximum resident/ {printf "%d", $1/1048576}' time.err)
    if [[ "$out" == "$(cat ref-$project$SUFFIX.json)" ]]; then same=same; else same=DIFFERS; fi
    label=warm; [[ $i == 0 ]] && label=cold
    echo "$project $label ${real}s ${rss}MiB $same"
  done
done

#!/bin/zsh
# Usage: cold.sh <runs> <binary>... — interleaved extract runs with the cache on (a --cache-dir per project, its parse
# caches warm) but no kept checker answer: what recording the checker's reads and keeping its answer cost a cold run.
# Lines in ab.sh's format for med.py.
runs=$1; shift
cd /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/extract-speed
for i in $(seq $runs); do
  for bin in "$@"; do
    for project in gate-large chakra-only; do
      case $project in
        gate-large) src=../gate-large/src ;;
        chakra-only) src=../checker-default/chakra-only/src ;;
      esac
      rm -f kept-cache/$project/checker-answers.msgpack
      out=$(/usr/bin/time -l $bin extract --src $src --json --quiet --cache-dir kept-cache/$project 2>&1 >/dev/null)
      real=$(echo "$out" | awk '/real/ {print $1}')
      rss=$(echo "$out" | awk '/maximum resident/ {printf "%d", $1/1048576}')
      cpu=$(echo "$out" | awk "/real/ {print \$3+\$5}")
      echo "$project $(basename $bin) ${real}s ${rss}MiB cpu=${cpu}s load=$(sysctl -n vm.loadavg | awk "{print \$2}")"
    done
  done
done

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A/B speed and memory of this checkout (or a branch) against origin/main, for when a change touches the resolver.

Builds both in release mode, then times `extract --json` in the Storybook addon's configuration (dependencies loaded,
cache on after a warm-up run, inherited props not collapsed) over Mantine and Chakra with their dependencies installed
(`scripts/corpora.py setup --corpus mantine --corpus chakra`; without them nothing would be loaded, so the run stops)
with the two builds interleaved and alternating which goes first, and prints the median wall time and peak RSS of each
side. The 1.10x time and 1.20x memory thresholds come from a calibration made with dependency loading and the cache
off (within 1.04 for time and 1.12 for memory with nothing changed); it has not been repeated in this configuration, so
treat them as a starting point. Nothing enforces them.

Usage: scripts/bench.py [BRANCH] [--runs N] [--corpus NAME]...   (BRANCH defaults to this checkout, uncommitted work included)
"""
import argparse
import os
import shutil
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
            head_tree = ROOT
            if args.branch:
                head_tree = os.path.join(tmp, 'head')
                git('worktree', 'add', '--detach', head_tree, git('rev-parse', '--verify', f'{args.branch}^{{commit}}'))
                trees.append(head_tree)
            build(head_tree, target, os.path.join(tmp, 'head-bin'))
            builds = {'base': os.path.join(tmp, 'base-bin'), 'head': os.path.join(tmp, 'head-bin')}
            corpora_dir = os.path.abspath(corpora.DEFAULT_DIR)
            print(f"{'corpus':<9} {'base ms':>8} {'head ms':>8} {'ratio':>6}   {'base MiB':>8} {'head MiB':>8} {'ratio':>6}")
            for corpus in corpora.selected(args.corpus):
                src = corpora.ready(corpus, corpora_dir, sparse=False)
                if not src:
                    sys.exit(f"{corpus['name']}: dependencies not installed, so none would be loaded; "
                             f"run `scripts/corpora.py setup --corpus {corpus['name']}`")
                command = lambda binary: extract_command(binary, src, os.path.join(tmp, 'cache-' + os.path.basename(binary)))
                samples = {'base': [], 'head': []}
                for label, binary in builds.items():
                    run_once(command(binary))
                for i in range(args.runs):
                    for label in (('base', 'head') if i % 2 == 0 else ('head', 'base')):
                        samples[label].append(run_once(command(builds[label])))
                median = {label: (statistics.median(s for s, _ in runs) * 1000, statistics.median(r for _, r in runs))
                          for label, runs in samples.items()}
                (bt, br), (ht, hr) = median['base'], median['head']
                print(f"{corpus['name']:<9} {bt:8.0f} {ht:8.0f} {ht / bt:6.2f}   {br:8.0f} {hr:8.0f} {hr / br:6.2f}")
        finally:
            for tree in trees:
                subprocess.run(['git', 'worktree', 'remove', '--force', tree], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

def build(manifest_dir, target_dir, destination):
    subprocess.run(['cargo', 'build', '--release', '--locked', '-p', 'caliper-docgen', '--manifest-path',
                    os.path.join(manifest_dir, 'Cargo.toml'), '--target-dir', target_dir], check=True)
    shutil.copy(os.path.join(target_dir, 'release', 'caliper-docgen'), destination)


def extract_command(binary, src, cache_dir):
    """The addon's configuration (packages/storybook/src/provider.ts): dependencies loaded, the cache on, and
    inherited props never collapsed. Each side keeps its own cache directory so one build never reads the other's. The
    checker answers, as it does by default."""
    return [binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json', '--load-dependencies', '--collapse-inherited-props', 'none',
            '--cache-dir', cache_dir]


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument('branch', nargs='?')
    parser.add_argument('--runs', type=int, default=9)
    parser.add_argument('--corpus', action='append')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    args.corpus = args.corpus or ['mantine', 'chakra']
    subprocess.run(['git', 'fetch', '-q', 'origin', 'main'], cwd=ROOT)
    target = os.path.join(ROOT, 'target')
    trees = []
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        try:
            base_tree = os.path.join(tmp, 'base')
            git('worktree', 'add', '--detach', base_tree, git('rev-parse', '--verify', 'origin/main^{commit}'))
            trees.append(base_tree)
